key_insight: MolHIT introduces a hierarchical discrete diffusion framework that generates molecular graphs in a coarse‑to‑fine manner, enabling more chemically valid and property‑aligned molecules than prior graph diffusion approaches.
problem_solved: Existing graph diffusion models for molecular generation suffer from low chemical validity and poor control of desired molecular properties, limiting their usefulness compared with 1D (SMILES) models.
method: Hierarchical discrete diffusion: generate molecular graphs progressively from coarse structure to fine atom/bond details to stabilize sampling and capture multi-scale structure.
Discrete denoising tailored to categorical graph features (nodes/edges) with a specially designed noise schedule and denoiser network.
Training and architectural strategies to preserve chemical constraints and steer generation toward target properties (e.g., valency-aware modules, conditional guidance).
impact: MolHIT makes graph-based molecular generation more reliable and controllable, helping AI/ML practitioners produce chemically realistic candidates for drug discovery and materials design while enabling property-focused generation workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: coarse-to-fine hierarchical diffusion stages (graph levels) with arrows showing denoising flow.
Before/after bar chart: chemical validity and property-alignment metrics comparing MolHIT vs prior graph diffusion baselines.
Molecule gallery: example molecules generated at each hierarchical stage (coarse structure → final molecule) to illustrate refinement.
Ablation/heatmap: effect of key components (hierarchy, discrete noise, constraint modules) on validity and property scores.
paper_title: MolHIT: Advancing Molecular-Graph Generation with Hierarchical Discrete Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Hojung Jung, Rodrigo Hormazabal, Jaehyeong Jo, Youngrok Park, Kyunggeun Roh
